market_mistake: The market prices the GLP-1 category as if demand is peaking and as if the incumbent duopoly's economics are the category's economics. The second growth phase is demand-side: affordability and access expansion, supply-constraint resolution, oral formulations, direct-to-patient distribution, generic entry after key expiries, and a chronic induction-to-maintenance treatment model — volumes UP while manufacturer net pricing COMPRESSES and share FRAGMENTS. The mistake is customer-side: reading price compression and share fragmentation as category weakness when they are the signature of an access-driven second demand phase — and pricing every position in the drug value chain off the incumbents' price curve, when the best equity may be an incumbent with underestimated volume/revision upside, a next-generation asset, or the manufacturing and access infrastructure.
null_thesis: Demand has in fact peaked: volumes flatten as the early-adopter cohort saturates and discontinuation stays high (no durable chronic-maintenance model), access expansion stalls at the payer wall, orals and next-generation assets disappoint, and the incumbent duopoly holds share and net price. The category's economics remain the duopoly's economics — no second phase arrives, and neither incumbents on volume, next-gen entrants, nor the manufacturing/access infrastructure re-rate on this driver.

first_confirming.trigger: At the incumbents' next quarterly prints — LLY (late Oct 2026) and NVO (early Nov 2026) — incretin franchise VOLUMES (units/scripts, not dollars) GROW while disclosed net price per unit COMPRESSES: the phase-2 signature (access-driven volume with price give-up) in a single print. The prints land on schedule regardless; only the reading is uncertain.
first_confirming.basis: one scheduled print cycle — both incumbents report by mid-Nov 2026; operator-approved shape 2026-08-31 (the names are the composition's inference, flagged in the note)

falsifiers.trigger: The demand peak CONFIRMS: incumbent incretin franchise volumes (units/scripts, not dollars) FLATTEN or decline across two consecutive quarterly prints — the second growth phase fails on volume.
falsifiers.basis: three-plus quarterly print cycles of the incumbent franchises (Q3'26, FY'26, Q1'27 all land inside the window); operator-selected 2026-08-31

falsifiers.trigger: Access expansion STALLS: coverage/reimbursement expansion and direct-to-patient channel volumes stall or reverse at the payer wall — the access driver of the second phase dies.
falsifiers.basis: payer coverage disclosures + the incumbents' direct-to-patient channel disclosures across the 2026-2027 guidance cycle; operator-selected 2026-08-31

note: Every judgment field traces to the operator: mechanism (customer-side) and both falsifiers selected 2026-08-31 from an offered set — the pricing-power and share-fragmentation falsifiers were offered and NOT selected; the operator kept the demand-side legs. market_mistake / null_thesis composed from the operator's stated thesis (2026-08-29: no demand peak; second growth phase on affordability/access, supply resolution, orals, direct-to-patient, generics, chronic induction-to-maintenance; volumes up, pricing compressed, share fragmenting; best equity possibly incumbent volume upside, next-gen assets, or infrastructure). first_confirming follows the operator-approved scheduled-print shape; LLY and NVO as the incumbent representatives are the composition's inference from the operator's 'incumbent' class (the NVDA precedent), flagged here — NVO is a non-US filer (the FPI readiness ruling stands open), named only as a disclosure to read, never a universe action.
